content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [product_name] connected to an HMI screen and communication is working fine between them. However, I would like to know how to modify a timer value in the [product_name] from the HMI screen.

You need to create an entry field in [product_name]. Assign this input to a free word in the VM area of the [product_name], for example, VW80. Then, in the [product_name], read this value using an analog network input and reference it to your timer.
Great, thank you for your help.
Hi, an easier approach: Map the time directly to VWx. Just write into VWx from the HMI. This way, there is no need to use an analog amplifier or additional analog inputs for referencing.
A new question posted by [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread titled 'What happens to the timer setting if the connection between HMI and [product_name] fails?'. Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user established communication between a [product_name] and an HMI screen, but needs guidance on changing timer values remotely via the HMI. Responses clarify that timer values can be written from the HMI into a specific memory word in the [product_name] and then referenced by the timer. Later replies offer a simplified workflow by mapping the timer value directly, suggesting that the overall process for parameter adjustment from HMI could be more user-friendly, leading to further discussion of alternative solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to easily modify or set timer values in the [product_name] directly through the HMI interface.
